prompt_en: A layered medium-wide documentary photograph at blue hour after rain on a windswept coastal moor. An oblique camera at heather height aligns rooted base, trace, ruler, and face. One unmistakably adult woman works as a field researcher beside a storm-wet, salt-worn boulder. One distinctive rock remains visibly rooted in its precise terrain site, and a single enormous hand-shaped trace occupies one exposed rock face. Presented as a legendary rock trace as physical site evidence, one anomalous trace is materially continuous with the rock surface. One broad palm hollow connects continuously to five separate finger grooves. The five grooves vary in length and spread naturally from the same palm. Raking light and salt grain show how trace contour depth and weathering establish a contact-shaped event. Their crushed, salt-paled mineral edges interrupt the darker weathered rock skin. Beside the ruler, a human hand body or tool makes the trace scale readable. The researcher holds a rigid measuring scale directly across the palm hollow, and numbered evidence markers follow all five fingertip ends. At the wet heather landmark, a witness measurement or landmark frames the rock as site evidence. The absent maker is legible through the stone's connected grip deformation. The frame withholds the maker. Every groove edge carries the same salt-paled compression through unbroken stone grain. Her legible face has long near-black wavy hair with a center part and soft face-framing strands, brown almond-shaped eyes, straight softly defined brows, fine dark eyeliner, warm-neutral skin, and muted rosy lips.
